 * Master's degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry or Physics or related field with 6+ years of experience; or a PhD with 3+ years' experience; or equivalent experience

 * Ability to work independently, high degree of flexibility and capable to work in a crossfunctional environment

 * In-depth understanding of Statistical Process Control (SPC) and/or Design of Experiments (DOE)

 * Working knowledge of statistical analysis and problem-solving methodologies
 * Experience with statistical tools (JMP, Minitab, etc.)

Our Product Engineers are domain experts first, developers second. They build Engines - the simulations and models that capture how buildings actually behave - fast, and increasingly with AI. But these prototypes live on GitHub and only run on laptops: untested against the platform, unavailable to customers.

That's the gap you close. You're the key counterpart to our Product Engineers: you understand what an Engine computes, how, and why - well enough to decide where each piece belongs, hand off what belongs to other teams, and build the rest yourself. No finished spec lands in your inbox. You read other people's code, ask the right questions, and turn a working prototype into a service we can run and trust. We work in a strongly agentic way - so will you.

Your mission
 * Run our Engines and make them better - correct, fast, observable. When results look wrong, you can tell whether it's the data, the integration, or the physics.

 * Onboard new prototypes - understand the method and edge cases; judge what's production-ready and what needs a rewrite.

 * Find the right home for each function - decompose monoliths and define the interfaces and data contracts that make those boundaries real.

 * Integrate - with Planning and our Systems Architects, translating between domain and platform language, then build what remains yourself.

 * Make the next Engine easier than the last - shape the conventions that let prototypes arrive closer to integration-ready.

You won't do this alone: DevOps, App/Experience, AI, and Data & Flows already own their domains.

Your profile
 * Several years of professional software engineering across the stack, centre of gravity in the backend.

 * Python and TypeScript - strong in one, comfortable in the other, attached to neither.

 * The ability to read and judge code you didn't write, including scientific and numerical code.

 * A low-ego, collaborative style with domain experts, and the skill to explain trade-offs to people who think in physics, not architecture.

 * Professional English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

Nice-to-have

 * Geometry in code (computational geometry, meshes, CAD or BIM/IFC).

 * Simulation and numerical methods (thermal/energy simulation, FEM/CFD, solvers).

 * Real experience with AI and agentic workflows.

 * Productionizing research or prototype code (ML pipelines, scientific computing, quant models).

 * Building-industry or energy-domain exposure.

Why us?
 * Real impact. The Engines you integrate don't sit in a demo - they feed real investment decisions and move the platform forward in tangible ways.

 * The full solution chain. From digital twin to performance monitoring - you work across a complete product portfolio, not isolated one-off projects. Every Engine you bring in has a real place in the whole.

 * Flexible working models. Home-office option and a modern office in the heart of Vienna.

 * And the day-to-day works too. Daily meal allowance (€5/day), regular team events, free snacks.

 * Compensation: €60,000 - €75,000 gross/year, depending on your experience.

About us
OPTIMUSE is a Vienna-based AI startup revolutionizing the real estate and construction industry. We bring insights to the world's largest asset class that it never had before - both for new developments and existing portfolios. Our AI Hans delivers instant, deep engineering insight into costs, risks and optimization potential, grounded in building physics, simulation and engineering. 1 Senior Research Engineer - Cross-Platform Microfabrication Processes (all genders) As part of the European Chips Act, Silicon Austria Labs (SAL) is driving innovation in quantum and semiconductor technologies through its Pilot Lines. 

Join our interdisciplinary teams at the interface of technology and fabrication and enjoy Villach's exceptional quality of life in the heart of the Austrian Alps. Be part of something bigger. Be part of Silicon Austria Labs.

The role is part of the new Pilot Line Operations (PLO) Team within the Microsystem Division. PLO is a multidisciplinary engineering team bridging research and pilot-line operations, combining microfabrication expertise, process integration, documentation and coordination between Research Units and the SAL cleanroom infrastructure.

Your future tasks include:
 * Hands-on execution of microfabrication processes across lithography, deposition, etching, cleaning, metrology and other relevant process modules.
 * Develop, integrate, troubleshoot and optimize complex microfabrication process flows, including cross-tool and cross-module interactions.
 * Execute and lead fabrication runs, analyze results and identify process integration issues, deviations and root causes: pilot-line runs, MPWs, technology demonstrators and external fabrication activities.
 * Assessing Technology and pilot-line maturity.
 * Work directly with scientists to translate new research concepts into fabricable process flows and experimental process runs.
 * Work closely with cleanroom tool owners and engineers to ensure compatibility with tool capabilities, cleanroom constraints and operational requirements.
 * Define and maintain process documentation, flow diagrams, process specifications, run sheets, recipes, track of changes and lessons learned.
 * Help establish standardized ways of working for process development, integration, documentation, qualification and scale-up.
 * Platform Specialization: Focusing primarily on one of the key Microsystems technology platforms (Quantum Technologies, Photonics, PiezoMEMS, Magnetic Microsystems) but operating across multiple projects.

Your profile:
 * MSc/PhD in microelectronics, microsystems, semiconductors, physics or a related field.
 * 5+ years of hands-on experience in semiconductor, MEMS, photonics or microfabrication technology, preferably in a cleanroom industrial environment.
 * Demonstrated expertise in fabrication process development and integration, with the ability to execute and troubleshoot processes. 
 * Broad understanding of multiple microfabrication modules and their interactions, rather than expertise limited to a single process step. 
 * Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to move between hands-on cleanroom work, process engineering, documentation and coordination. 
 * Strong organizational and documentation skills for technical reporting and professional documentation. 
 * Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively while supporting multiple stakeholders.
 * Excellent teamwork, communication, reporting, and organizational skills. 
 * Excellent oral and written communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Important Facts about SAL:
 * Diverse research activities with many technical challenges.
 * State-of-the-art laboratory facilities and equipment.
 * Location in the heart of Europe in Austria - relocation support for non-European nationalities.
 * Internal and external training opportunities for career development.
 * Family & children friendly - actively shaping the compatibility of family and career.
 * "Vital4SAL" to promote a healthy workplace (e.g. SAL coaching pool, trainings on mental health, physical activities, healthy snacks, 24/7 accident insurance)
